$comment: Seam ledger — every upstream file this fork modifies, with why. See FORK.md §3. Checked by scripts/check-fork-divergence.mjs. Seams are divergence we carry knowingly at every upstream sync (standing rule: contributions upstream are the exception, decided by Matthieu, and only for what genuinely serves GeoLibre); keep them rare and small.

seams.reason: branding-v1: fork README — presents Geospatial Studio, states and links the GeoLibre parentage, keeps upstream's useful links attributed to GeoLibre; upstream's README describes their distribution channels (stores, PyPI, hosted apps), not this repo.
branding-v1: tab title, apple-mobile-web-app-title, description, theme-color -> Geospatial Studio

branding-v1: brand block -> <BrandMark/> (src/branding/), ds-topbar class for the all-caps menu voice; branding-v2: Help command destinations/keywords follow Geospatial Studio and hosted builds omit the irrelevant upstream release checker

branding-v2: About presents Geospatial Studio as the product, explicitly credits and links GeoLibre upstream, uses Dynamik-owned destinations, and omits release checks from centrally deployed web builds
branding-v2: Help labels About as Geospatial Studio and hides the desktop release checker from centrally deployed web builds
branding-v2: Help website, repository, and feedback destinations are sourced from the fork-owned branding/product module
branding-v2: English product identity and explicit GeoLibre fork attribution for the Geospatial Studio About surface
branding-v2: the configurable Help/About entry uses the Geospatial Studio product label
branding-v1: one @import of src/branding/branding.css (fonts, dark surfaces, top-bar typography)
branding-v1: PWA manifest name/short_name/description/theme_color -> Geospatial Studio
branding-v1: manifest.name assertion follows the rebrand
branding-v1: asset swap — D lettermark tab icon (32px)
branding-v1: asset swap — D lettermark tab icon (32+48px ICO)
branding-v1: DEFAULT_BASEMAP -> OpenFreeMap Dark (was styles/liberty). The product's standard view is 2D on a dark basemap.
branding-v1: empty-workspace projection defaults to 2D — DEFAULT_STARTUP_SETTINGS.globeByDefault and the normalize fallback both -> false (was true/globe).
branding-v1: startup projection assertions follow the 2D default (globeByDefault false -> mercator).
branding-v1: built-in basemap substitution assertion follows DEFAULT_BASEMAP -> dark.
branding-v1: exported-story projection assertion follows the 2D default (globe -> mercator).
branding-v1: pixel assertions wait for the remote dark basemap to settle and compare premultiplied-alpha Lighten against that dark backdrop rather than upstream's light-basemap normal composite.
